active_themes.label: Warsh's Impossible Choice
active_themes.summary: Flat April spending (0% MoM, released May 29) confirms demand is weakening under prior tightening, while PCE inflation holds at 3.4%—the exact stagflation setup Warsh hoped to avoid. He must choose between pausing cuts (admitting his inflation narrative was wrong) or continuing cuts into weakening demand (risking a credit cascade). The bond market has already priced this as negative; the Fed will have clarity forced upon it within two weeks as lenders begin announcing tightening.

active_themes.label: Deal Remains Decision-Critical
active_themes.summary: Today's Iran deal relief rally briefly lifted oil sentiment, but the underlying damage is done: $88-90+ oil over the past week has already compressed consumer balance sheets. Even if a deal closes, Warsh gets only tactical breathing room—the key test is whether June spending (released July) stabilizes or deteriorates further. Negotiations remain fragile; collapse within 48 hours would re-spike oil to $95+ and trigger immediate policy crisis. The next 72 hours remain outcome-determinant.

active_themes.label: Credit Cascade Imminent
active_themes.summary: Today's flat spending print provides lenders with explicit cover to accelerate withdrawal. The three-week silence on deposit rate cuts from major players (Discover, Capital One, Amex) is likely to break within 5-10 days. If they announce tightening, the credit feedback loop accelerates and equities face 3-5 day reset downward. If silence persists through next week, it signals they believe today's weakness is transitory—but data does not support that bet.

active_themes.label: Binary Resolved, Wrong Direction
active_themes.summary: The May 29 spending print (0% MoM) confirmed the second scenario: institutional withdrawal was justified and soft landing is no longer the base case. Today's modest market gains reflect intraday tactical relief on Iran and AI, not conviction about macro. Equities have not yet repriced this fully and face a reset over the next 3-5 days as the credit tightening becomes explicit.

active_themes.label: Stagflation Pricing In
active_themes.summary: Today's flat spending + 3.4% inflation validates the stagflation scenario: Warsh is cutting rates into a demand-weakening environment while inflation remains elevated. The 30-year yield at 2007 highs reflects this and is unlikely to move lower absent a hard demand shock. Long-duration investors are positioned for extended elevated rates; expect 10-year yields to hold 3.9-4.1% range through next data cycle.
